structure.heading: Social Impact, Diversity Outcomes, and Board Oversight of Sustainability Commitments (FY2024)
text_content: **Social Impact, Diversity Outcomes, and Board Oversight of Sustainability Commitments (FY2024)**

In FY2024 the company recorded 0.32 TRIR and 0.08 LTIR across 8.6 million hours worked, demonstrating focus on operational safety and risk mitigation. Safety performance was supported by enhanced field supervision, quarterly safety audits, and a training program that delivered 22,400 instructor-led and e-learning hours. Incident investigations resulted in 14 corrective action plans implemented by year-end. These measures align with our occupational health targets and provide a baseline for FY2025 improvement initiatives tied to contractor management and digital reporting.

As of 31 Dec 2024, women represented 41% of the global workforce and 33% of leadership (Director+), reflecting progress against our gender inclusion objectives. During FY2024 we expanded leadership development and mentorship programs, introduced an annual pay-equity review, and funded community education initiatives benefiting 12,000 participants. Retention improvements were concentrated in early-career cohorts, and the company established measurable targets for FY2025 to increase representation at Director+ levels through targeted external recruitment and internal promotion.

As of 31 Dec 2024 the Board had 10 directors, 70% independent, 40% women, and 30% underrepresented minorities, providing diverse oversight of ESG performance and public commitments. The Board’s Sustainability Committee meets quarterly, reviews progress against our decarbonization roadmap, social programs, and executive incentives tied to sustainability KPIs, and reports annually to shareholders. Board-level escalation protocols were used to resolve two compliance issues in FY2024.

structure.heading: Decarbonization Performance and Scope 1–3 Inventory Results (FY2024)
text_content: In FY2024 the company's operational emissions inventory reports Scope 1 emissions of 42,180 tCO2e and Scope 2 (market-based) emissions of 18,640 tCO2e, for a combined Scopes 1 and 2 total of 60,820 tCO2e. Scope 3 emissions are reported at 612,900 tCO2e. This inventory follows the GHG Protocol guidance and was subject to internal review and third‑party assurance of material categories to support transparency and comparability across reporting periods, published in the FY2024 sustainability report.

Against the 2019 baseline of 78,500 tCO2e (Scopes 1+2 market-based), the company achieved a 22% reduction by FY2024. This progress reflects energy efficiency investments, fuel switching in fleet operations, and procurement of renewable electricity under market‑based contracts. Targeted capital projects implemented during FY2022–FY2024 delivered the majority of reductions, while ongoing initiatives include expanded on‑site renewables, operational electrification pilots, and annual performance tracking to align with the company’s long‑term net zero commitment and climate resilience.

Scope 3 represents the largest portion of the FY2024 inventory at 612,900 tCO2e, led by Purchased Goods & Services at 402,300 tCO2e and Business Travel at 21,700 tCO2e. The company has prioritized supplier decarbonization, sustainable procurement standards, and travel policy revisions to reduce these categories. Planned FY2025 actions include supplier emissions data collection, lifecycle assessment integration in sourcing decisions, and supplier collaboration pilots, with progress monitored quarterly and reported annually to the Sustainability Committee.

No material compliance breaches; 3 minor whistleblower cases resolved.
Linking 20% of executive bonus to emissions + safety KPIs (effective FY2026).
Overall assessment: credible pathway to 50% absolute emissions reduction by 2030.
